question: Under NTEP, which of the following best describes the legal obligation for TB notification in India?

answers.text: Notification is voluntary and encouraged for public-sector providers only.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Notification is mandatory, not voluntary, and applies to all healthcare providers including the private sector.

answers.text: All diagnosed TB cases must be notified to the government through Ni-kshay; this is a mandatory legal requirement for both public and private providers.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Since 2012, TB was made a notifiable disease in India. All cases — irrespective of sector — must be reported through the Ni-kshay portal. Non-compliance is a legal offence.

answers.text: Only smear-positive pulmonary TB cases require notification; extrapulmonary TB is exempt.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. All forms of TB — pulmonary, extrapulmonary, drug-resistant — must be notified. Restricting notification to smear-positive cases would miss a large proportion of the TB burden.

answers.text: Notification is required within 30 days of diagnosis.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Ni-kshay notification should happen at the time of diagnosis and treatment initiation, not within 30 days. Timely notification is essential for contact tracing and programme monitoring.

overallFeedback.feedback: Revisit the prevention and programme section. Under NTEP, all TB cases must be notified through Ni-kshay — this is a legal mandate for both public and private providers.
Excellent. Mandatory Ni-kshay notification for all TB cases is a non-negotiable NTEP obligation that every clinician must know.
